newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Dutch-based firm pulls out of Kyrgyz gold project.
newsitem.headline: Dutch-based firm pulls out of Kyrgyz gold project.

text.p: Netherlands-registered Silk Road Gold Corp has stopped prospecting work on the Nikchesu goldfield in the former Soviet republic of Kyrgyzstan, an official from state gold concern Kyrgyzaltyn said on Monday.
"Silk Road Gold spent a season doing exploration work on Nikchesu, looking for a large goldfield," Valentin Bogdetsky, a senior adviser with Kyrgyzaltyn, told Reuters in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek.

"But having done some drilling, the company did not find what it had expected and considered further work pointless," Bogdestsky said, adding that Kyrgyzaltyn still thought the gold field held promise.
Alexander Yarkov, in charge of Kyrgyzaltyn's joint venture activities, said that Nikchesu also contained antimony and complex ores.
"To implement such projects, one needs a complex approach, while Silk Road Gold was interested only in the extraction of gold," Yarkov said.
He declined to give estimates of Nikchesu's reserves but some experts put them at 158 tonnes of gold and 88,000 tonnes of antimony.
Kyrgyz officials say Silk Road Gold is free to take part in other gold projects.
Last year, Canada's Cameco Corp began extracting gold from Kyrgyzstan's largest goldfield, Kumtor, which has estimated reserves of 514 tonnes.
Cameco, better known as a large uranium producer, has invested $452 million in Kumtor. It owns one third of the mine while Kyrgyzaltyn owns the remaining two thirds. --Almaty Newsroom +7 3272 509410
